 Davies Petrus - Senior Editorial Staff 
 Share 
4 Min Read 
 SHARE 
 Chef Damodharan , popularly known as Chef Damu , died on Sunday at the age of 72, sending shockwaves through Tamil households and the Indian culinary world. The news, reported by The Times of India, highlights his long battle with ill health and his lasting impact as a TV judge, chef, and Padma Shri awardee. This article covers his rise from humble beginnings, his major achievements, and the legacy he leaves behind.

 From Kitchen Helper to Top Chef 
 National Honors and Records

 Key Takeaways
 Chef Damodharan rose from dishwasher to celebrated chef and Padma Shri awardee.
 He earned a PhD in Hotel Management and set a Guinness World Record.
 His death marks a big loss for Tamil television and Indian culinary circles.
 From Kitchen Helper to Top Chef
 Chef Damu started his career as a dishwasher in local restaurants, learning the basics of food preparation and kitchen discipline. He worked his way up, taking on roles as a line cook and eventually a head chef, gaining respect for his skill and hard work. His determination earned him a place in the Indian culinary scene, and he later became the first Indian chef to earn a PhD in Hotel Management from the University of Madras.The journey shows how perseverance can turn a modest start into a celebrated profession.
 National Honors and Records
 Throughout his career, Chef Damu collected several prestigious honors. He was awarded the Padma Shri, one of India’s highest civilian awards, for his contributions to the culinary arts and hotel management. He also set a Guinness World Record for preparing the most dishes in a single day, a feat that demonstrated his speed and expertise. These achievements cemented his reputation as a trailblazer in Indian cuisine.
 Television Fame on Cooku with Comali
 Chef Damu became a household name when he joined the Tamil reality show Cooku with Comali as a judge. On the show, he guided contestants through challenging kitchen tasks while adding humor and warmth to each episode. Viewers loved his easy‑going style and his willingness to share cooking tips with the audience.His presence helped the program become a staple of Tamil entertainment.
 Health Struggles and Final Days
 In recent years, Chef Damu faced serious health issues. He used a wheelchair after a hip fracture and knee surgery, and he missed the semi‑finals of Cooku with Comali Season 7 due to a leg injection. In a video message he told fans, “I am doing fine,” trying to reassure them despite his condition. The chef’s health continued to decline, leading to his passing at the age of 72.
 Legacy and Tributes
 Chef Damodharan leaves behind a rich legacy of culinary excellence, education, and television entertainment. He inspired many young chefs to pursue formal education and to aim for high standards in hospitality. His warmth on screen and his commitment to quality cooking will be remembered for years to come.Fans, colleagues, and the Tamil community have expressed deep sorrow and gratitude for his contributions.
